boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Providence College
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe food destinations in Providence with currently published late hours. Check the linked venue before heading out, since operating hours can change.

cards.title: Antonio's Pizza on Thayer
cards.subtitle: 256 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Use the official shop page to confirm the day’s closing time, then choose between a slice, whole pie, calzone, salad, wings, or dessert.
cards.short_summary: A College Hill pizza counter with published midnight-to-2 a.m. closing times.
cards.evidence_claim: Antonio's says its Thayer Street shop closes at midnight Sunday–Thursday and 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists 11 a.m. opening, midnight closing Sunday–Thursday, and 2 a.m. closing Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Baja's Tex Mex Grill
cards.subtitle: 273 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: This Thayer Street kitchen publishes daily late hours. Check the location page before leaving and use its listed phone number for a same-night confirmation.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street Tex-Mex option with a published 2 a.m. close.
cards.evidence_claim: Baja's lists its 273 Thayer Street location as open daily from 10 a.m. to 2 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official locations page lists this Providence site daily, 10 a.m.–2 a.m.

cards.title: Baja's Taqueria on Thayer
cards.subtitle: 227 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: For a separate Thayer Street stop, use Baja's Taqueria listing and verify the day: it posts midnight on weekdays and Sunday, with later weekend hours.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Baja's format with published midnight and weekend 2 a.m. closing.
cards.evidence_claim: Baja's lists its 227 Thayer Street Taqueria open until midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official locations page posts 10 a.m.–midnight Monday–Thursday and Sunday; 10 a.m.–2 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Caliente Mexican Grill
cards.subtitle: 267 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Plan a food-only stop on Thayer Street and consult the location page before going; it gives one daily schedule and a direct contact number.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street Mexican restaurant posting a daily 1 a.m. close.
cards.evidence_claim: Caliente's Providence–Thayer Street page lists hours seven days a week, 10 a.m.–1 a.m.
cards.source_title: Caliente Mexican Grill — Thayer Street Providence
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 10 a.m.–1 a.m., seven days a week.

cards.title: Chinatown on Thayer
cards.subtitle: 277 Thayer Street, Providence
cards.notes: Use the venue’s online ordering page for current availability and choose from its food menu; the listed schedule runs to 2 a.m. every day.
cards.short_summary: A Thayer Street Chinese-food destination with daily 2 a.m. posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Chinatown on Thayer's ordering page lists daily hours of 11 a.m.–2 a.m. at 277 Thayer Street.
cards.access_notes: The venue's Toast ordering page lists daily hours from 11 a.m. until 2 a.m.

cards.title: CILANTER
cards.subtitle: 168 Atwells Avenue, Providence
cards.notes: Check the restaurant’s ordering page before setting out. It lists a food menu with halal, vegan, and vegetarian choices alongside late daily service.
cards.short_summary: An Atwells Avenue food destination posting 2 a.m. closing every day.
cards.evidence_claim: CILANTER's ordering page lists 2 a.m. closing times every day at 168 Atwells Avenue.
cards.access_notes: The venue's ordering page lists 2 a.m. closing Sunday–Saturday, with day-specific opening times.

cards.title: Haven Brothers Diner
cards.subtitle: 12 Dorrance Street, Providence
cards.notes: Head downtown for the stainless-steel diner trailer and verify the nightly schedule first; its official contact page distinguishes weeknight from Friday–Saturday closing times.
cards.short_summary: A mobile diner destination with published closing times after 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Haven Brothers lists 5 p.m.–2:30 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 5 p.m.–3:30 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official contact page lists Sunday–Thursday 5 p.m.–2:30 a.m.; Friday–Saturday 5 p.m.–3:30 a.m.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies
cards.subtitle: Providence
cards.notes: Use the official store page to select the local shop and confirm pickup or delivery availability for the night before placing a cookie order.
cards.short_summary: A Providence cookie shop whose official store page advertises delivery until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies' Providence store page states that warm cookies are delivered until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Official Providence store page advertises warm-cookie delivery until 3 a.m. daily; confirm the selected store's service area at checkout.

cards.title: Sicilia's Pizza
cards.subtitle: 181 Atwells Avenue, Providence
cards.notes: For a Federal Hill pizza option, check the restaurant’s official ordering location before leaving; the page posts separate late takeout hours by day.
cards.short_summary: An Atwells Avenue pizzeria with officially posted late takeout hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Sicilia's official location page lists takeout until 2 a.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday, and until 3 a.m. Friday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists takeout Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–2 a.m., Friday 10 a.m.–3 a.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–midnight, and Sunday noon–3 a.m.

cards.title: Vasilios Pizza
cards.subtitle: 579 Atwells Avenue, Providence
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s official site to confirm the nightly schedule and order food for pickup or delivery; it posts especially late closing times on most nights.
cards.short_summary: An Atwells Avenue pizza restaurant posting 4 a.m. closing Monday–Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Vasilios Pizza lists hours of 10 a.m.–4 a.m. Monday–Saturday and 11 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Monday–Saturday 10 a.m.–4 a.m. and Sunday 11 a.m.–2 a.m.; it also advertises late-night delivery.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for studying, gathering, recreation, reflection, and student activities.

cards.title: Slavin Center
cards.subtitle: Providence College student union
cards.notes: Use the lounges or meet up before an event; student-organization offices, reservable rooms, and McPhail’s are all in the building.
cards.short_summary: The campus student union concentrates meeting space, services, and organization offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College identifies Slavin Center as its student union, with lounge space, ’64 Hall, McPhail’s, reservable rooms, and student-organization offices.
cards.access_notes: Community and visitor information is provided by the College; individual spaces may be reservable or have separate access rules.

cards.title: The Library’s 24/7 Space
cards.subtitle: Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring your PC card for an overnight work session; the space has flexible furnishings and a first-come, first-served group study room.
cards.short_summary: A card-access study area that remains available after the main library closes.
cards.evidence_claim: Phillips Memorial Library says its 24/7 Space provides PC students a safe overnight study space after midnight, with card-swipe access and a first-come group study room.
cards.access_notes: PC student card-swipe access is required; the page states access begins when the main library closes at midnight.

cards.title: John E. Fogarty Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Plan a research visit when you need primary sources: ask library staff about using archives, manuscript collections, rare books, or college-history materials.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built reading room for archives and special-collections research.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says students, faculty, staff, and community members may use the Fogarty Reading Room for Providence College Archives and Special Collections research.
cards.access_notes: Located on the library’s second floor; consult the library’s visiting information before an archives visit.

cards.title: Phillips Memorial Library Quiet Zones
cards.subtitle: First and second floors of Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Choose a marked perimeter desk when you need low-noise focus; keep conversation minimal and use headphones for audio.
cards.short_summary: Clearly marked silent-study areas around the library’s first- and second-floor perimeters.
cards.evidence_claim: Phillips Memorial Library designates Quiet Zones on its first and second floors for silent study and asks patrons to minimize talking and use headphones.
cards.access_notes: Use the clearly marked zones and follow the library’s quiet-use expectations.

cards.title: Ruane Center for the Humanities
cards.subtitle: Academic building on campus
cards.notes: Pause between classes to orient yourself in the humanities core; courses in Development of Western Civilization, English, and history meet here.
cards.short_summary: A 63,000-square-foot academic building connecting humanities programs and classrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College states that the Ruane Center for the Humanities houses Development of Western Civilization, Liberal Arts Honors, English, and history courses.
cards.access_notes: Primarily an academic building; classroom availability and access may vary with the class schedule.

cards.title: Ray Dining
cards.subtitle: Raymond Dining Hall
cards.notes: Meet classmates over a meal or use a table for a study break; check Dining Services for the current menu and operating schedule.
cards.short_summary: The campus dining hall offers breakfast, lunch, and dinner seven days a week during regular operations.
cards.evidence_claim: Dining Services describes Ray Dining as a place where students meet friends and study, with 15 dining options and regular breakfast, lunch, and dinner service.
cards.access_notes: Dining access requires an applicable meal plan, swipe, guest pass, or payment; schedules vary during breaks.

cards.title: Peterson Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation complex
cards.notes: Check the recreation schedule, then use the facility for intramurals, the track, racquetball, group fitness, or pool time as available.
cards.short_summary: The central recreation complex includes Begley Arena, racquetball courts, a pool, and fitness space.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College calls Peterson Recreation Center the hub of intramural, athletic, and recreational activity and lists Begley Arena, Cuddy Racquetball Complex, and Taylor Natatorium.
cards.access_notes: Available to undergraduate students and recreation members; individual facilities and times may vary.

cards.title: Concannon Fitness Center
cards.subtitle: Peterson Recreation Center complex
cards.notes: Use the cardio and strength areas for a scheduled workout, or check recreation information before planning a group session or indoor cycling visit.
cards.short_summary: A two-level fitness facility with cardio equipment, strength machines, free weights, and an indoor cycling studio.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College lists dedicated fitness space on two levels at Concannon, including cardio equipment, strength machines, free weights, and an indoor cycling studio.
cards.access_notes: Facility use is for the membership population; the College posts hours and notes that holiday schedules may change.

cards.title: Schneider Arena
cards.subtitle: Campus ice arena
cards.notes: Look for a student skating activity or a hockey event, and confirm the event’s entry details before heading to the arena.
cards.short_summary: The campus ice arena hosts varsity hockey as well as student skating and intramural hockey activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College’s Student Handbook states that Schneider Arena is home to men’s and women’s ice hockey and provides student activities including ice skating and intramural hockey.
cards.access_notes: Skating sessions, games, and other activities are scheduled separately; confirm availability and any ticketing requirements.

cards.title: St. Dominic Chapel
cards.subtitle: Providence College campus chapel
cards.notes: If you want a Sunday evening faith gathering, check Campus Ministry details and arrive for Last Chance Mass, followed by its food-and-fellowship event.
cards.short_summary: The campus chapel hosts the College’s Sunday 10 p.m. Last Chance Mass.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College documents Last Chance Mass at 10 p.m. on Sundays in St. Dominic Chapel, followed by the Post-Mass Bash.
cards.access_notes: Service and related-event details can change; verify the current Campus Ministry schedule before attending.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten documented no-admission or no-purchase activities for Providence College students, on campus and around Providence.

cards.title: Play pool at McPhail’s
cards.subtitle: McPhail’s Entertainment Facility, Slavin Center
cards.notes: Bring a friend to the ground level of Slavin Center and use one of McPhail’s two pool tables; the College says table use is always free.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost pool-table break inside the student center.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College states that use of McPhail’s pool tables is always free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Located in McPhail’s, Room G10 on the ground level of Slavin Center; intended for Providence College students.

cards.title: Share free popcorn at McPhail’s
cards.subtitle: McPhail’s Entertainment Facility, Slavin Center
cards.notes: Meet in McPhail’s for popcorn before a campus program, game watch, or conversation; the student handbook says popcorn is always free of charge.
cards.short_summary: A simple, documented free snack stop in Lower Slavin.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College states that popcorn at McPhail’s is always free of charge.
cards.access_notes: McPhail’s is on the ground level of Slavin Center and is a campus student facility.

cards.title: Ride RIPTA with your PC ID
cards.subtitle: RIPTA routes serving Providence
cards.notes: Use your Providence College ID for a no-fare ride, then plan a daytime stop downtown, on College Hill, or at a public cultural destination.
cards.short_summary: Campus ID unlocks fare-free public-transit rides.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College says all Providence College students can ride RIPTA free of charge with their PC ID.
cards.access_notes: Carry a valid Providence College ID; check RIPTA for current routes and service times.

cards.title: Take a historic library tour
cards.subtitle: Providence Public Library, 150 Empire Street
cards.notes: Reserve or walk into a scheduled Wednesday tour to explore the library’s historic and renovated spaces; confirm that a tour is running before you go.
cards.short_summary: A guided look through Providence Public Library’s building.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence Public Library offers free guided historic library tours on select Wednesdays at 11 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Tours begin at the 150 Empire Street entrance; the library recommends advance sign-up and checking its calendar.

cards.title: Tour the Rhode Island State House
cards.subtitle: Rhode Island State House, 82 Smith Street
cards.notes: Join the weekday 10 a.m. or 1 p.m. docent-led tour for a shared civic outing; reservations help, though walk-ins are welcome at those times.
cards.short_summary: A free, docent-led visit inside Rhode Island’s State House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rhode Island Secretary of State offers free docent-led State House tours Monday through Friday at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Weekday public tours are free; submit a request at least one business day ahead when possible or walk in at the listed tour times.

cards.title: Walk Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.subtitle: 282 North Main Street, downtown Providence
cards.notes: Take a conversation-paced loop through the memorial grounds and visitor center, then use the site as a starting point for nearby historic streets.
cards.short_summary: A downtown national memorial with no entrance fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that there is no fee or entrance pass required to access Roger Williams National Memorial.
cards.source_title: Fees & Passes — Roger Williams National Memorial
cards.access_notes: No entrance pass is required; check the National Park Service page for current visitor-center information.

cards.title: See the RISD Museum on Sunday
cards.subtitle: RISD Museum, 20 North Main Street
cards.notes: Plan a Sunday gallery visit with friends and give yourselves time to browse the collection; reserve the museum’s designated free Sunday ticket before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Sunday museum browsing with no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: RISD Museum states that admission is free on Sundays from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free Sunday admission is 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; the museum lists a Free Sunday Ticket among its admission options.

cards.title: Walk a WaterFire lighting
cards.subtitle: Waterplace Park and downtown riverwalks
cards.notes: Pick a scheduled lighting, meet downtown, and explore the riverwalk on foot together; use WaterFire’s event schedule for date-specific details.
cards.short_summary: A free public-art evening along Providence’s rivers.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire Providence states that admission to all WaterFire lightings is free.
cards.access_notes: Admission is free; optional donations and paid vendor offerings are separate. Confirm the lighting schedule before travel.

cards.title: Browse the WaterFire Arts Center gallery
cards.subtitle: WaterFire Arts Center, 475 Valley Street
cards.notes: Visit during published gallery hours and take in the current exhibition at your own pace; check the calendar because exhibitions and programs change.
cards.short_summary: Free rotating art exhibitions in the Valley neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire Providence states that WaterFire Arts Center gallery admission is free and open to all.
cards.access_notes: The cited page lists gallery hours and says admission is free; donations are encouraged and events may have separate details.

cards.title: Visit the Bell Gallery
cards.subtitle: List Art Building, 64 College Street
cards.notes: Make a daytime art stop at Brown’s Bell Gallery and look through the current exhibition together; verify opening hours before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A free contemporary-art gallery on College Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Brown University describes the David Winton Bell Gallery as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: David Winton Bell Gallery at Brown University
cards.access_notes: The cited Brown page lists the gallery at 64 College Street and describes it as free and open to the public; verify current exhibition hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct Providence College study environments, with official details on quiet work, research, collaboration, computers, and access.

cards.title: 24/7 Student Study Space
cards.subtitle: Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use your PC card after the main library closes; choose flexible furnishings for an overnight session, then claim the first-come group room if needed.
cards.short_summary: Card-access study space with flexible furniture and a first-come group room.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says this PC-student space uses card-swipe access from midnight when the main library closes and includes a first-come, first-served group study room.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces | Phillips Memorial Library | Providence College
cards.access_notes: For PC students; card-swipe access begins at midnight when the main library closes.

cards.title: John E. Fogarty Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Bring a research question and work with archival or special-collections materials in this second-floor reading room; ask library staff about visiting procedures.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading room for Archives and Special Collections research.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College identifies the second-floor Fogarty Reading Room as a place to conduct research using its Archives and Special Collections.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces | Phillips Memorial Library | Providence College
cards.access_notes: Students, faculty, staff, and community members may visit; consult the library's visiting guidance for collection use.

cards.title: First-Floor Quiet Zones
cards.subtitle: Phillips Memorial Library, perimeter seating
cards.notes: Set up at the first-floor perimeter when you need low conversation and headphone-friendly focus; follow the posted quiet-zone expectation while you work.
cards.short_summary: Marked perimeter study areas intended for quiet individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Phillips Memorial Library says its first-floor perimeter includes clearly marked Quiet Zones where patrons are expected to minimize talking and use headphones for audio.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces | Phillips Memorial Library | Providence College
cards.access_notes: Located around the first-floor perimeter; keep talking to a minimum and use headphones for audio.

cards.title: Second-Floor Quiet Zones
cards.subtitle: Phillips Memorial Library, perimeter seating
cards.notes: Head upstairs for a marked quiet-zone seat and keep audio in headphones; it is a practical setting for reading, drafting, or other solo work.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor marked quiet areas with a low-conversation expectation.
cards.evidence_claim: Phillips Memorial Library lists clearly marked Quiet Zones around its second-floor perimeter and asks patrons to minimize talking and use headphones for audio.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces | Phillips Memorial Library | Providence College
cards.access_notes: Located around the second-floor perimeter; keep talking to a minimum and use headphones for audio.

cards.title: Library Conference Room
cards.subtitle: First floor, Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Reserve by email for a planned team session, or check whether it is open first-come; connect a laptop to the room screen for shared review.
cards.short_summary: Reservable first-floor room with a laptop-connected presentation screen.
cards.evidence_claim: The first-floor Library Conference Room is reservable or first-come, first-served and has a screen with laptop connectivity.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces | Phillips Memorial Library | Providence College
cards.access_notes: Reserve by emailing pmlconferenceroom@providence.edu, or use it first-come, first-served when available.

cards.title: The TreeHouse
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Phillips Memorial Library
cards.notes: Use the cozy windowed space for a study group or a short reset, and pair your visit with nearby advising, writing, or tutoring resources.
cards.short_summary: Windowed community study space near core academic-support services.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College describes the TreeHouse on the library's second floor as a place for studying and study groups near Academic Advising, the Writing Center, and Tutoring Services.
cards.source_title: Multicultural Student Success | Academic Services at Providence College
cards.access_notes: The page lists Monday–Friday hours of 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. and notes an adjusted weekend schedule.

cards.title: Palmisano Atrium
cards.subtitle: Ryan Center for Business Studies
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative project to the two-story atrium, where the building is designed for study and collaboration; use the open setting for group planning.
cards.short_summary: A two-story atrium designed as study and collaboration space.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College says the Ryan Center's two-story atrium functions as study and collaboration space, and identifies the atrium as part of its expansive study and event spaces.
cards.source_title: Students, faculty make Ryan Center for Business Studies a ‘home’ | PC News
cards.access_notes: Located in the Arthur F. and Patricia Ryan Center for Business Studies; confirm building availability before a visit.

cards.title: Accinno Hall 202 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Accinno Hall 202
cards.notes: Choose this lab when you need a campus desktop rather than your own device; plan around the handbook's listed daily computer-lab hours.
cards.short_summary: An 18-computer lab with published evening and weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College's student handbook lists Accinno 202 as a computer lab with 18 personal computers and published Sunday-through-Saturday hours.
cards.access_notes: Handbook lists: Sunday 9 a.m.–midnight; Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–midnight; Friday 8 a.m.–8 p.m.; Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Howley Hall 321 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Howley Hall 321
cards.notes: Use one of the listed desktops for software-based coursework or a focused digital work block; check the daily lab schedule before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A 24-computer study lab with late weekday hours listed by the College.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College's student handbook lists Howley 321 as a computer lab with 24 personal computers and published daily hours.
cards.access_notes: Handbook lists: Sunday noon–midnight; Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–midnight; Friday 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

cards.title: Koffler Hall 118 Computer Lab
cards.subtitle: Koffler Hall 118
cards.notes: Settle in at a campus computer for individual digital work, and use the listed evening schedule to fit a study block around class or meetings.
cards.short_summary: A 29-computer lab with scheduled evening and weekend availability.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College's student handbook lists Koffler 118 as a computer lab with 29 personal computers and published daily hours.
cards.access_notes: Handbook lists: Sunday noon–midnight; Monday–Thursday 8 a.m.–midnight; Friday 8 a.m.–6 p.m.; Saturday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along Federal Hill, Spruce Street, Atwells Avenue, Valley Street, and Sims Avenue.

cards.title: Pass beneath La Pigna
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Start at the gateway arch, then continue along Atwells Avenue to orient yourself to the Federal Hill commercial corridor.
cards.short_summary: A named Federal Hill gateway and street-side landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The Federal Hill Commerce Association identifies La Pigna as the gateway arch over Atwells Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public landmark; verify conditions before visiting.

cards.title: Pause at DePasquale Square
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue and DePasquale Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Use the square as a walking pause between Atwells and Spruce, and check its current public programming before you go.
cards.short_summary: A named square at the center of the Federal Hill streetscape.
cards.evidence_claim: GoProvidence lists DePasquale Square at Atwells and DePasquale Avenues in Providence.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public square; programming and access can vary.

cards.title: Pick up a dessert from Pastiche
cards.subtitle: Spruce Street corridor, beside Atwells Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a takeout stop at 92 Spruce Street; the bakery says its cakes, slices, and pastries are prepared on-site daily.
cards.short_summary: A takeout bakery on the Spruce Street side of Federal Hill.
cards.evidence_claim: Pastiche lists 92 Spruce Street and says it prepares cakes, slices, and pastries on-site daily for takeout.
cards.access_notes: Takeout-only bakery; confirm current hours before traveling.

cards.title: See Scialo’s brick-oven bakery
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Stop at 257 Atwells Avenue for the bakery’s bread, savory pies, pastries, and cookies; check its posted day-by-day hours.
cards.short_summary: A Federal Hill bakery with a documented brick-oven tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Scialo Bros. Bakery lists 257 Atwells Avenue and describes products including bread, savory pies, pastries, and cookies.
cards.access_notes: Retail bakery; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Choose a takeout stop at Chef Ho’s
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Use Chef Ho’s at 243 Atwells Avenue for its listed dine-in, takeout, or delivery options; confirm service availability first.
cards.short_summary: A named Chinese restaurant on the Atwells Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Chef Ho’s lists its Federal Hill address as 243 Atwells Avenue and offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant; confirm current hours and ordering options before visiting.

cards.title: Browse Venda Ravioli’s store
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Walk to Venda’s listed Atwells Avenue store for a market-style food stop, and use the business’s contact page for current hours.
cards.short_summary: A named food-store destination on Atwells Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Venda Ravioli’s official contact page lists its store at 275 Atwells Avenue in Providence and provides current daily hours.
cards.access_notes: Retail food store; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Watch for Gather’s glass demos
cards.subtitle: Atwells Avenue corridor, Federal Hill
cards.notes: Check Gather’s schedule for its listed live glass demos or classes, then pair the visit with a café or ice-cream stop if desired.
cards.short_summary: A café and glassworking destination at the western end of Atwells.
cards.evidence_claim: Gather lists its Federal Hill location at 519 Atwells Avenue and advertises glassblowing classes and live demos.
cards.source_title: Gather Cafe & Ice Cream Bar Location
cards.access_notes: Classes and demonstrations may require scheduling; verify availability.

cards.title: Check WaterFire Arts Center exhibits
cards.subtitle: Valley Street corridor, Valley/Olneyville
cards.notes: Look up the current exhibition or event calendar before heading to the Arts Center’s large Main Hall at 475 Valley Street.
cards.short_summary: WaterFire’s permanent multipurpose arts venue in the Valley area.
cards.evidence_claim: WaterFire identifies the Arts Center at 475 Valley Street as its headquarters and a multipurpose arts venue with a 15,000-square-foot Main Hall.
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions and events vary; verify current public access and any ticketing.

cards.title: See what Wilbury is staging
cards.subtitle: Valley Street corridor, inside WaterFire Arts Center
cards.notes: Review Wilbury’s current production calendar before visiting its performance space inside the WaterFire Arts Center at 475 Valley Street.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit theatre company sharing the Valley Street arts venue.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wilbury Theatre Group lists its location as 475 Valley Street inside the WaterFire Arts Center and describes producing new works and reimagined classics.
cards.access_notes: Performance dates and ticket requirements vary; confirm details in advance.

cards.title: Look for a Steel Yard class
cards.subtitle: Sims Avenue corridor, Valley/Olneyville
cards.notes: Check the Steel Yard’s current public classes and events before traveling to its metalworking and industrial arts campus on Sims Avenue.
cards.short_summary: A named industrial-arts destination near the Valley Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Steel Yard identifies itself as a Providence industrial arts center offering public classes and events at 27 Sims Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Class registration, event access, and age policies may vary; verify before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Providence College rituals and recurring campus practices, from the shared Civ finish line to the Senior Ring Weekend Mass.

cards.title: Learn the Alma Mater by Senior Year
cards.subtitle: Providence College song tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the college hymn set to Sibelius’s “Finlandia,” then join in when you know the words; the college says many students sing it with pride by senior year.
cards.short_summary: A shared hymn of thanksgiving and confidence in divine providence.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College identifies its alma mater as a hymn set to a movement from Sibelius’s “Finlandia” and says students often sing it by senior year.
cards.access_notes: No attendance, cost, or public-access terms are stated on the source page.

cards.title: Mark the Finish Line for Civ
cards.subtitle: Development of Western Civilization shared experience
cards.notes: Complete the Development of Western Civilization sequence, then take part in the college’s named Done With Civ celebration with others reaching the same milestone.
cards.short_summary: A celebration tied to finishing Providence College’s shared Civ experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College states that students celebrate completing Development of Western Civilization with a Done With Civ celebration.
cards.access_notes: Participation details and any event-specific costs are not stated on the source page.

cards.title: Bring Your People to Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual fall campus gathering
cards.notes: Plan around the fall Homecoming Weekend, when the college convenes students, alumni, families, faculty, pets, and friends for Friar-centered events.
cards.short_summary: A fall reunion weekend built around the wider Friar community.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College describes Homecoming as a fall gathering of students, alumni, families, faculty, pets, and friends, anchored by special events.
cards.access_notes: Specific dates, registration, and costs are not stated on the source page.

cards.title: Take the Friar 5K Route
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Weekend event
cards.notes: If the event is offered during Homecoming, join the Friar 5K as a daytime campus activity and confirm the year’s route and registration details with the college.
cards.short_summary: A named running event that anchors Providence College Homecoming.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College lists the Friar 5K among the special events anchoring Homecoming Weekend.
cards.access_notes: The source does not provide current route, registration, cost, or participation requirements.

cards.title: Catch the Homecoming Madness
cards.subtitle: Homecoming Weekend event
cards.notes: Watch for the college’s Late Night Madness programming during Homecoming Weekend, and use the official event listing for the year’s time, location, and entry guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named Homecoming event in Providence College’s annual gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College lists Late Night Madness as one of the special events anchoring Homecoming Weekend.
cards.access_notes: The source confirms the event’s Homecoming role but gives no current late-hours, location, cost, or entry details.

cards.title: Play for the Championship T-Shirt
cards.subtitle: Providence College intramural sports tradition
cards.notes: Form a team for an intramural season and aim for the championship T-shirt, which the college identifies as a coveted piece of clothing on campus.
cards.short_summary: A campus sports tradition centered on the intramural champion’s shirt.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College describes an intramural championship T-shirt as a coveted item on campus.
cards.access_notes: Season schedules, eligibility, and any fees are not stated on the source page.

cards.title: Make Time for Last-Chance Mass
cards.subtitle: Providence College campus worship tradition
cards.notes: Check the college’s campus-ministry schedule for the next Last-Chance Mass and participate respectfully if it fits your practice and plans.
cards.short_summary: A named campus Mass included among Providence College’s Friar traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College includes Last-Chance Mass in its published selection of Friar traditions.
cards.access_notes: The source names the tradition but does not state schedule, location, public access, or cost.

cards.title: Spot Friar Dom and Huxley
cards.subtitle: Providence College mascots
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for Providence College’s two named mascots, Friar Dom and Huxley, at campus gatherings and document the encounter with a respectful photo.
cards.short_summary: The pair of named mascots woven into Friar campus life.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College’s traditions page identifies its mascots as Friar Dom and Huxley.
cards.access_notes: Appearance times and locations are not stated on the source page.

cards.title: Receive the Ring at Senior Ring Weekend
cards.subtitle: Class-ring rite of passage
cards.notes: Follow the Senior Ring Weekend committee’s official instructions; the weekend includes social events and concludes with Mass, ring blessing, and distribution.
cards.short_summary: Providence College’s class-ring weekend and culminating blessing.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College calls Senior Ring Weekend a rite of passage and says it includes a black-tie ball plus blessing and distribution of class rings at Mass.
cards.access_notes: This is intended for seniors; the source does not state current dates, registration, ticketing, or costs.

cards.title: Carry the Black-and-White Tassel Forward
cards.subtitle: Class Mass and graduation keepsake
cards.notes: At the class Mass described by the college, receive and keep the black-and-white tassel as a reminder of the years leading to graduation.
cards.short_summary: A tassel given at a class Mass and saved for graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College says students receive a black-and-white tassel at a Mass with their classmates and keep it for graduation.
cards.access_notes: Class eligibility, timing, location, and any associated costs are not stated on the source page.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Providence College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A ten-stop, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence centered on campus orientation, arts, recreation, faith, and student programming.

cards.title: Start by locating Harkins Hall
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival · campus bearings
cards.notes: Use Harkins Hall as a first landmark: the Admission Office is on its first floor, making it a concrete place to begin learning campus routes.
cards.short_summary: Anchor your first walk around a major campus building.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College states that its Office of Admission is located on the first floor of Harkins Hall.
cards.access_notes: Use the College’s interactive campus map and follow campus access instructions.

cards.title: Make a daytime café stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Ruane Center for the Humanities
cards.notes: If you arrive during weekday service, pause at Ruane Café for a beverage or quick bite before continuing toward the library and east campus.
cards.short_summary: A weekday café stop inside the Ruane Center for the Humanities.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruane Café is in the Ruane Center for the Humanities and offers beverages, pastries, and Simply to Go meals.
cards.access_notes: The dining page lists regular hours as Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–3 p.m.; it is closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: Find the library before you need it
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · academic landmarks
cards.notes: Walk to Phillips Memorial Library and note its approach from the Ruane side of campus; it is a useful landmark for future study breaks.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to a central academic destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College’s campus map lists Phillips Memorial Library as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Consult the interactive campus map for current routing and building access.

cards.title: See the current Reilly Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Smith Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Check the gallery’s current exhibition listing, then visit Reilly Gallery during posted hours for a low-key arts stop on the east side of campus.
cards.short_summary: A free public gallery visit in the Smith Center for the Arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College Galleries identifies Reilly Gallery at the Smith Center for the Arts, says its galleries are free and open to the public, and posts gallery hours.
cards.access_notes: The gallery page lists Reilly Gallery hours and asks visitors to enter campus through Huxley Gate; confirm current exhibition dates before going.

cards.title: Check for a free campus concert
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Smith Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Review the Music Department calendar and, when a program is scheduled, head to Ryan Concert Hall for an evening performance with classmates.
cards.short_summary: Use the music calendar to add a performance to the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College’s Music Department says its events are free and open to the public and are held in Ryan Concert Hall unless otherwise noted.
cards.access_notes: Check the current calendar before attending; the page gives Smith Center entry and parking directions.

cards.title: Look for a Board of Programmers event
cards.subtitle: Friday night · Lower Slavin 12
cards.notes: Check the Board of Programmers’ current listings or stop by its Lower Slavin office to learn what student-planned programming is on this weekend.
cards.short_summary: Connect with recurring student-run campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College says its Board of Programmers plans campus events and that its Weekend Programming committee provides activities Friday through Sunday nights.
cards.access_notes: The office is listed as Lower Slavin 12, across from McPhail’s; verify the specific event’s time and entry details.

cards.title: Put Schneider Arena on your map
cards.subtitle: Saturday · recreation and ice activities
cards.notes: Find Schneider Arena during a daytime campus loop, then check student recreation announcements if an ice-skating or intramural hockey activity is offered.
cards.short_summary: A campus arena associated with hockey and student ice activities.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Handbook identifies Schneider Arena as home to Providence College’s hockey teams and says it also provides student activities such as ice skating and intramural hockey.
cards.access_notes: Availability depends on the activity schedule; consult current student recreation information before planning a skate.

cards.title: Explore recreation options at Peterson
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · campus recreation
cards.notes: Visit the Peterson Recreation Center area and look into the current intramural sign-up process if you want a social activity beyond your first weekend.
cards.short_summary: A starting point for intramural and recreation involvement.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College identifies the Peterson Recreation Center as the site of much intramural and recreation activity, including the Begley Arena, racquetball complex, and natatorium.
cards.access_notes: Current participation procedures and facility availability may vary; check Recreation’s current intramural information.

cards.title: End Sunday with Last Chance Mass
cards.subtitle: Sunday, 10 p.m. · St. Dominic Chapel
cards.notes: If it fits your interests, join the Sunday 10 p.m. Last Chance Mass in St. Dominic Chapel, then stay for the listed post-Mass food and fellowship.
cards.short_summary: A documented Sunday-night campus faith and community gathering.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College describes Last Chance Mass as a Sunday 10 p.m. Mass in St. Dominic Chapel followed by the Post-Mass Bash.
cards.access_notes: Providence College lists this gathering at Sunday 10 p.m.; confirm current liturgical scheduling before attending.

cards.title: Save Friar Nite Ride for the trip back
cards.subtitle: Thursday–Saturday nights · campus and surrounding neighborhood
cards.notes: For an eligible late-night trip on campus or nearby, use Friar Nite Ride rather than walking alone; keep the service window saved on your phone.
cards.short_summary: A late-night shuttle option for Providence College students.
cards.evidence_claim: Providence College’s 2025–2026 Student Handbook describes Friar Nite Ride as a late-night shuttle for PC students traveling on campus and in the surrounding neighborhood.
cards.access_notes: The handbook lists service Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights from 7 p.m. to 3 a.m.; confirm any current operating updates before relying on it.
